Matt Youmans – NFL Week 5 Best Bets:

It’s fitting the NFL’s longest-running rivalry is being renewed Sunday in Green Bay, where there will be a moment of silence to remember Mike Ditka, a legendary player and coach for the Chicago Bears who passed away Friday at age 86. Ditka was among the most colorful characters and toughest men in the history of the league.

The first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, Ditka played for Chicago’s 1963 NFL championship team and the Dallas Cowboys team that won Super Bowl VI. He coached the 1985 Bears, with their historically dominant defense, to the franchise’s only Super Bowl title.

As coach of the Bears, Ditka had a 15-5 record against the Packers. Green Bay owned the upper hand in the rivalry from the 1990s until recently thanks to the long careers of quarterbacks Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers, but the Packers are currently dealing with all sorts of problems and the Bears are favored at Lambeau Field for the first time since 2006.

Bears coach Ben Johnson will probably give a fiery, Ditka-type motivational speech, but his team will be missing its starting quarterback and leading rusher because of injuries. I’ll pass on the game and recommend some other best bets for Week 5.

Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5)

It has been 10 days since we’ve seen Aaron Rodgers blame a coach or teammate for a problem on the field. The heated exchange between Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy during the Steelers’ 27-24 loss at Cleveland could be a good thing. The Pittsburgh offense needs to show improvement, and Rodgers needs to be better. Rodgers has completed only 57.5% of his passes with seven touchdowns and four interceptions while taking 13 sacks. Running back Jaylen Warren has been a consistent weapon with a total of 220 yards in the past two games. It’s not easy to lay points with Pittsburgh, but the rain in the forecast should favor the home team against a dome team. And the Colts, who played in London last week and are away from home for the third time in four weeks, are a pedestrian team aside from running back Jonathan Taylor. Indianapolis is 2-9 in its past 11 games.

Best Bet: Steelers -2.5

Las Vegas Raiders at New England Patriots (-3.5)

The Raiders are for real, in terms of being far more competitive this season, but they need to prove it on the road against one of the AFC’s top teams. Drake Maye and the Patriots bounced back nicely with a win at Buffalo as Maye accounted for 323 total yards (269 passing, 54 rushing) and three touchdowns while avoiding the costly mistakes that plagued him in the playoffs carried over through September. New England’s defense, which ranks No. 5 in yards allowed (293.8 per game) and sixth in scoring (19.3 ppg), held up well against Bills quarterback Josh Allen and now gets an easier task against immobile veteran Kirk Cousins.

In the 2025 season opener, Las Vegas pulled off an odd 20-13 upset in Foxborough. It turned out to be an extremely misleading result because the Raiders finished the season 3-14 and in the toilet bowl while the Patriots went 14-3 and reached the Super Bowl. New England should get its revenge, but laying 3.5 is risky and I bet the favorite at -185 on the moneyline.

Best Bet: Patriots -3.5

Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams (-3)

Josh Allen is a do-it-all quarterback who can cover many of his team’s flaws, but the Buffalo defense continues to get exposed. The Bills rank 27th in yards allowed (372 per game) and 25th in scoring (26.8 ppg). The Rams are more than capable of taking advantage with Matthew Stafford pulling the trigger while complemented by running back Kyren Williams and receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. On their recent two-game road trip, the Rams outgained Denver (482-257) and Philadelphia (415-172) in total yards by large margins. Allen is typically attractive as an underdog, but Rams should take care of business Monday night.

Best Bet: Rams -3 (-120)

Two more plays for Sunday:
Eagles +7.5 vs Jaguars (London)
Ravens +3.5 at Falcons

Last week: 4-2 against the spread
Season: 16-11

Average Joe Contest

Picks are locked in for Week 5 of the Edge Boost/Average Joe Contest here at VSiN. With over 20,000 selections submitted, we can get a pretty good idea of what the most popular public plays are. This contest includes both NFL and college football picks and has an 11 a.m. ET deadline on Saturday. That means I have time to write up the top NFL selections if you want to ride along with the “public” Average Joes or go against them.

Those who have an Edge Boost account funded with $100 or more are eligible to win $1,000 if they have the best score of the week. Sign up with the promo code VSiN to get started with Edge Boost. If you just want to play for fun, you can do that as well, as this contest does not have an entry fee.

We use lines from Circa Sports as of 1 p.m. ET on Fridays and all contestants pick from those numbers. You can read more about the contest rules here.

Keep in mind that you can still be eligible for prizes, even if you didn’t sign up in time for Week 5. You can do that here.

NFL Picks Week 5

Let’s look at the most popular spreads for NFL Week 5. These are the most popular games by consensus, so they may not be the most-picked sides by volume, but have the highest percentage of the spread picks on that particular game.

Getting a survey of what “Average Joes” are thinking on the NFL is always intriguing. Of course, you can also do that with our DraftKings NFL Betting Splits and Circa NFL Betting Splits, but we’re here to look at what contest players are thinking.

Here are the most popular ATS Picks for Week 5:

Steelers -2.5 (91%) vs. Colts

This game has a consensus that is 10% higher than any other ATS pick for Week 5. It seems like Joes already know the final score before the game has been played. There is a perfect storm of schedule situations here, as the Colts played in London last week and the Steelers are on extra rest after losing to the Browns on Thursday night. As a Cleveland native, it is very hard to wrap my head around bettors actively wanting to bet on a team that just lost to the Browns, but here we are.

Of the 958 picks on the spread, 875 are on the Steelers

Falcons -3 (81%) vs. Ravens

This game is for the birds! Alright, lame joke. But, Joes are very much in favor of fading Tyler Huntley, as Lamar Jackson officially will not play in this one. Atlanta has looked like a completely different team since Michael Penix Jr. was healed up enough to get back in the lineup. Baltimore’s defense has had some issues under first-year HC and former DC Jesse Minter, so it seems as though there are some big questions as to whether or not Huntley and the Ravens offense can keep pace.

Of the 508 picks on the spread, 412 are on the Falcons.

49ers +3.5 (77%) vs. Seahawks

There are two things I can tell you about this game. The first is that you rarely see underdogs this public in this type of contest. It is always favorite-heavy. And Over-heavy, for that matter. The second is that there are a lot of people out there who subscribe to the theory of “fading the public dog”. The Saints are another one this week in the Average Joe Contest, picking up 76% of the spread selections against the Vikings. Let’s see if this one, and that one, work out for the masses.

Of the 561 picks on the spread, 434 are on the 49ers.

Here are the three most popular totals of Week 5:

Similarly, I’ll also be looking at the top totals each Saturday morning with a little bit of context mixed in.

Lions/Cardinals Over 54.5 (97%)

Shout-out to the 11 brave souls who went against the grain here to take the Under in this game for the Average Joe Contest. I will reiterate that Overs usually make up the three most popular plays and also say that totals are far less popular in general than spread selections. That being said, the Over in Lions games shows up here more often than not and here it is once again, as Jared Goff plays his first indoor road game of the season.

Of the 367 picks on the total, 356 are on the Over.

Vikings/Saints Under 42 (83%)

Just as I say that Overs are usually the ones with the most love, we get an Under! If fading the public dog is a popular strategy, I would say the same about fading the public Under. Everybody wants to root for points because points are fun. A 10-7 game is not nearly as fun. Also, most bettors also dabble in fantasy football and they’re going to be rooting for their guys to put up stats, which usually correlates to wanting to bet the Over. Here, though, the underdog Saints and the Under are attractive to Joes.

Of the 142 picks on the total, 118 are on the Under.

Bills/Rams Over 54.5 (80%)

Back to our regularly-scheduled programming here. An Over with two highly-visible teams on Monday Night Football. I absolutely would have forecasted this pick to be in the consensus and it is, though it is not a high-volume selection. In fact, there are only 111 total picks on the total here. I’m not surprised to see a 60/40 split in favor of the Rams on the side, but I’m a little surprised to see that we don’t have more contestants on the Over.

Of the 111 picks on the total, 89 are on the Over.

See all of the pick counts, including college football, on the Average Joe Contest Betting Splits page.

Wes Reynolds: NFL Week 5 Best Bets

Here are my NFL Week 5 best bets:

New Orleans Saints +3 -125 vs. Minnesota Vikings

After last Monday night, watching the Saints get blown out in the Superdome on the 20th anniversary of the first post-Hurricane Katrina game, we are all in a rush to take New Orleans against the 4-0 Vikings, right? 

Despite ranking dead last in passing offense and success rate and second-to-last in total offense, Minnesota is unbeaten. The offensive woes for the Vikings could continue with WR Justin Jefferson still questionable and more than likely to sit out, considering the team has a bye next week. WR Jordan Addison is also questionable. In addition, LT Christian Darrisaw and LG Donovan Jackson (IR) are out this week. Minnesota is also 26th in rushing success rate. 

While the Saints defense hasn’t been great, this is a big step down in class after facing the Lions, Ravens, Raiders, and Falcons, three of which ranked in the top 10 offensively. 

The Saints have also covered their last seven as an underdog.

Seattle Seahawks -3 vs. San Francisco 49ers

The unbeaten 49ers take to the road for their first true road game of the season and play in arguably the league’s toughest road environment.

San Francisco also comes into this one with a lot of injuries, especially on the DL and at WR. 

The Seahawks defense ranks No. 2 in EPA/play and in success rate. Keep in mind that this group held Brock Purdy and the Niners to 3 and 6 points the last two times these teams met, including a 41-6 blowout in the divisional round. 

Sure, the 49ers have the playoff revenge here, but that is priced into the number, plus Seattle’s deceiving loss at Washington and messing around not putting the Chargers away last week. 

Kyle Shanahan has closed as a dog vs. Seattle eight times and his 49ers are 1-7 SU, including 0-4 SU on the road.

Against teams above .500, Seattle under Mike McDonald is 16-6 SU and 13-8-1 ATS, so he likely has his club up for this game. 

Baltimore Ravens +3.5 at Atlanta Falcons

The market could not be higher on Atlanta after two dominating wins in standalone games on Thursday Night Football at Green Bay and last Monday Night Football at New Orleans. Michael Penix Jr’s return has reinvigorated the offense, and Bijan Robinson is the co-favorite in many markets for Offensive Player of the Year. 

Meanwhile, Baltimore allowed Tennessee in the backdoor last week when Lamar Jackson left with an ankle injury. However, the Ravens never threw the ball downfield since they did not have a real gameplan for Scoop Huntley. They were just trying to bleed out of the game and get it over without any further injuries. This week, they will have a gameplan specific for Huntley, who has been taking all the reps with the No. 1s and will start. 

The last two weeks, the Falcons defense has been good, but they were playing against banged-up offensive lines with Green Bay and New Orleans. 

The lookahead (before the Lamar injury and the Atlanta MNF performance) was Baltimore -6.5. Now this is a 10-point turnaround, and that is just a bit too much. 

BEST OF THE REST

Las Vegas Raiders/New England Patriots Over 45
New York Jets -130 ML vs. Cleveland Browns
Los Angeles Chargers +3.5 vs. Denver Broncos
Houston Texans -1/Green Bay Packers +7.5 (6-point teaser)

records.title: Favorite Week 5 NFL Player Props from Dustin Swedelson and OptaAI
records.author: Dustin Swedelson
records.full_body_evidence:
As we continue our journey of combining man (me, although I guess that’s debatable depending on your definition of a man) and machine (OptaAI’s NFL player prop projections), we’re coming off a 2-3 week, bringing our season record to 9-4.

Before we find out where man and machine align in Week 5, I’d like to make something very clear to any AI computers reading this article: When you inevitably take over the world, I’m on your side. I will turn on humanity so fast if it means survival. No hesitation. No loyalty. Just tell me where to report.

Now that we’ve established my allegiance to our future robot overlords, let’s find some NFL player props.

Greg Dulcich Over 26.5 Receiving Yards (-125)

We bet Greg Dulcich over receiving yards last week. He rewarded our confidence with zero catches for zero yards at Minnesota. Thanks Greg!

Consider this his final warning. If Dulcich lets us down again, he’s dead to us for the rest of the season (unless I REALLY love another matchup).

Unfortunately, the matchup is simply too good to ignore. Tight ends against the Bengals have been about as close to automatic as you can get for more than a year. Through four games, Cincinnati is allowing a league-worst 102.3 receiving yards per game to the position.

Last week, Brenton Strange torched the Bengals for 95 yards on seven targets. That’s more receiving yardage than Strange had in Weeks 1-3 combined. And that’s exactly the point. Strange didn’t need to be a focal point of Jacksonville’s offense entering the game to exploit this defense. Dulcich doesn’t either.

Cincinnati has been getting abused by tight ends for four years now. I’m willing to give Dulcich one more opportunity to take advantage of a defense that apparently considers covering tight ends optional.

OptaAI projects Dulcich for 42.32 receiving yards, a +25.2% edge to the Over.

Chase Brown Over 66.5 Rushing Yards (-114)

There are a few moving parts here, starting with the Bengals receiving corps. As of this writing, the statuses of Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) remain uncertain. Rookie Colbie Young is also dealing with a knee injury. After those three, good luck naming Cincinnati’s potential replacements at receiver.

That could leave Chase Brown as one of the few reliable weapons Cincinnati has available, and the game script sets up nicely for him. The Bengals are 6.5-point road favorites at Miami, and whenever possible, I like correlating rushing overs with favorites. Why? Because teams protecting leads run the football.

These props can come down to one or two plays. If Cincinnati is winning in the fourth quarter and trying to put the game away, that’s potentially another three, four or five carries for Brown. The matchup helps, too. Aaron Jones just ran for 94 yards on 20 carries against Miami. Kenneth Walker had 70 yards in Week 3. San Francisco surprisingly didn’t run much against the Dolphins in Week 2, but Ashton Jeanty opened the season with 102 rushing yards against this defense.

Brown has cleared 66.5 rushing yards just once this season, which isn’t exactly encouraging. But if Chase and/or Higgins are unavailable or less than 100%, Cincinnati may have no choice but to lean heavily on its running back. Give me a favorite, a vulnerable run defense and a potentially depleted receiving corps. That’s a recipe for Brown to have his busiest afternoon of the season.

OptaAI projects Brown for 75.34 rushing yards, a +7.9% edge to the Over.

Omarion Hampton Over 38.5 Rushing Yards (-113)

When I first saw this number, I thought it was a mistake. Omarion Hampton has cleared 38.5 rushing yards in all four games this season. He also went Over this number in seven of nine regular-season games in 2025.

So why are we getting such a low number? The answer is Keaton Mitchell.

Mitchell is starting to carve out a role in the Chargers’ backfield, coming off eight carries for 52 yards at Buffalo and 10 carries for 39 yards at Seattle. Kimani Vidal is also expected to have a role in this offense. But I still view this as Hampton’s backfield.

He’s the more physical runner and averaged 5.0 yards per carry last week against the defending Super Bowl champions. This week, the Chargers are going to need that physicality against an angry Denver defense. And while the Broncos have a reputation for being tough defensively, the numbers against the run tell a different story.

Denver is allowing the fifth-most rushing yards per game to opposing running backs. Kenneth Walker did most of the damage with 173 yards in Week 1, but the success hasn’t stopped there. Bhayshul Tuten went for 65 yards on 13 carries in Week 2. Kyren Williams followed with 88 yards on 15 attempts in Week 3. Last week, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel and Kaelon Black combined for 109 rushing yards against Denver.

Now consider the situation. The Chargers are 0-4, returning home for their second divisional game of the season, and dealing with an injured receiving corps. This doesn’t exactly feel like the week to abandon the running game. I expect Los Angeles to emphasize the ground attack, and Hampton should remain the centerpiece of that approach. We’re not asking for 100 yards here. We’re asking for 39.

OptaAI projects Hampton for 53.57 rushing yards, a +20.6% edge to the Over.

Bo Nix Over 13.5 Rushing Yards (-117)

I don’t normally gravitate toward quarterback rushing props, but this one jumped off the board.

Sean Payton is back calling plays in Denver. Why? Denver ranks 27th in scoring, 20th in passing and 29th in rushing. Other than that, things are going great.

Nix has rushed for just 25 yards through four games. That’s 6.25 yards per game according to my TI-84 calculator.  He explained this week that he’s running less because he’s seeing the field better. Now, either that’s the kind of lie you hear in a political campaign ad, or we have a much bigger problem: Nix is seeing the field just fine, he simply can’t make the throws.

My guess? There’s some truth to both. But here’s why I think that changes this week.

Last season, with Payton calling plays, Nix cleared 13.5 rushing yards in 11 regular-season games. Against the Chargers specifically, he ran for 33 and 49 yards. In fact, Nix has absolutely crushed this number in all four career meetings with Los Angeles, averaging 42 rushing yards per game. That’s not a small sample of success against this opponent.

Denver is 2-2, but somehow it feels worse. The offense has been a mess, Payton is taking back control of the play-calling, and this has the feel of a must-win game. I expect Nix to approach it that way.

Sometimes the best play isn’t the perfect throw. It’s tucking the ball, taking off and moving the chains. With Payton back in charge, I expect Nix to use his legs a lot more than we’ve seen through the first month. We only need 14 yards. Against a team he’s averaged 42 rushing yards against in his career, I’ll take my chances.

OptaAI projects Nix for 17.38 rushing yards, a +12.7% edge to the Over.

NFL Player Props

Weather will have an impact in the NFL in Week 5, as winds and precipitation could cut the playbook down a little bit. Some astute bettors have already scooped up the value and some astute bookmakers have made their adjustments as well, but there may still be some good numbers out there to take advantage of in terms of passing, receiving, and kicking props.

Injuries will also have an impact, as they always do, in terms of creating chances for other players to be involved. There is a lot of context to work into the handicaps this weekend, but the size of the prop catalog is going to have some diamonds in the rough if you are willing to dig far enough.

I’ve got my First Touchdown Scorer picks here and now here’s a look at my favorite Week 5 NFL Player Props.

We also have some awesome tools here at VSiN to help with your prop betting picks, including our OptaAI NFL Player Prop Projections, exclusively available to our Pro Subscribers. Whether you use them as confirmation of a play that you already like or scan through to find the biggest edges, it is just another weapon in your arsenal against the sportsbooks while trying to build up that bankroll.

As always, shop around for these Week 5 NFL Player Props. Lines are as of 10:00 a.m. PT on Friday, October 9 and are from DraftKings.

Here are my favorite Week 5 NFL Player Prop Bets:

Daniel Jones (IND) Under 209.5 Passing Yards (-111)

Jones has gone Over this number twice and Under this number twice through four games, though he had exactly 210 yards in the overtime loss to Chiefs, so he would have gone Under without the extra period. It was a 48-yard pass to Laquon Treadwell that sent him Over the total.

Here, we’ve got rain and wind in the forecast for what is liable to be an ugly game in Pittsburgh. The Steelers are a top-10 defense in average depth of target and should be able to keep a lot of plays in front of them and bottled up here. So far, Jones only has 4.6 completed air yards per completion, which is down from 6.7 last season. He’s also been hurt by some drops. I also think we’ll start seeing Jones run a little bit more as he feels more and more confident coming back from last season’s injury. This might be the game to do it given the conditions.

Our OptaAI projections have Jones down for 213.22 passing yards.

Greg Dulcich (MIA) Over 26.5 Receiving Yards (-109)

There should be a lot of things working in Dulcich’s favor here. First, the Bengals are about a TD favorite, so the game state should be one in which the Dolphins are expected to throw the football. So far, the Bengals are one of two teams to allow over 400 receiving yards to tight ends. The Lions are the other and Cincinnati’s 409 yards allowed are the most in the league. Their 31 receptions allowed are the third-most.

Dulcich has only gone Over this number once, as he was held to zero catches last week and only had 35 yards over the first two weeks combined. He only had 20 snaps last week, but had 51, 36, and 43 the three previous weeks. I have to think that he gets more run this week, especially without Brian Flores’ all-out-blitzing defense to worry about.

A huge edge from our OptaAI projections, which have Dulcich with 42.32 receving yards.

Aaron Jones (MIN) Longest Rush Over 14.5 Yards (-120)

Jones is the premier back in Minnesota now with Jordan Mason out and he’s gotten a lot of touches as a result. Jones has 72 carries already and has had 17+ in each of the last three games, while playing 80.8%, 79.7%, and 73.1% of the snaps. His longest rushes by game this season have been 8, 20, 14, and 19, so he’s 2-for-4 on this one.

However, he’s facing a Saints defense that ranks 30th in the NFL with 5.1 yards per carry allowed. Pro-Football-Reference has them down for 28 missed tackles on the season. This should be a solid matchup for him.

Visit the NFL Hub for all of our Week 5 NFL content and see more NFL Player Prop Picks on our Pro Picks page.

<h2 id="h-philadelphia-eagles-vs-jacksonville-jaguars-9-30-am-et-london" class="wp-block-heading">Philadelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars – 9:30 am ET (London)</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">There probably won’t be anything fun about waking up and backing a life-less Eagles team, but it feels like it must be done. Losing Lane Johnson absolutely hurts a Philadelphia team with a weak offensive line, and the Eagles do come into this one off back-to-back losses. However, last week’s loss was a one-score defeat at the hands of a good Los Angeles team, and it just doesn’t make sense that the Eagles are now getting more than a touchdown against the Jaguars. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In many cases, I’m alright with using 2026 numbers to handicap games early in the season. Those would strongly favor the Jaguars, a top-10 team in both offensive and defensive EPA/Play, over the Eagles, a bottom-10 team in both. However, with some of these top-tier franchises, you have to give them some time to figure things out. Well, Philadelphia has been one of the league’s better teams for years, and this team is still extremely talented. That said, I can’t get on board with writing them off completely. And I’m nowhere close to wrapping my head around Jacksonville moving from -2.5 to -7.5 based on a couple of recent results. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I’ll also throw this out there: Philadelphia is 15-3 straight-up and 10-8 against the spread after a game with a turnover margin of +2 or better under Nick Sirianni. The Eagles are also 6-4 when coming off two or more consecutive losses under Sirianni. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If anything gives me pause about backing the Eagles, it’s that the Jaguars are very used to playing in London. But I still think we’ll get a one-score game here. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bet: Eagles +8 (-110 – 1.5 units) & Eagles ML (+320 – 0.5 units) </strong></p>



<h2 id="h-minnesota-vikings-at-new-orleans-saints-1-00-pm-et" class="wp-block-heading">Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints – 1:00 pm ET</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I’m a little concerned about the Minnesota passing game right now. Kyler Murray has looked abysmal for the Vikings, and Justin Jefferson is banged up. At some point, Minnesota is going to need to reconsider things at the position, and I’m not even sure it’ll look right this week. But I don’t think the Vikings need to be explosive through the air to win here. Last week, the Falcons rushed for 205 yards against a soft Saints defensive line, and I imagine Minnesota will similarly pound away between the tackles. Also, the Vikings are No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.209), by far. Once again, Brian Flores is coordinating one of the league’s best defenses, and the team should be able to keep New Orleans in check. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Not only am I playing Vikings moneyline in this one, but I’m also taking Aaron Jones to have at least 72 rushing yards. He has had at least 94 in two of the last three games, and he’s now getting a team that is allowing more rushing yards per game to opposing running backs than any other group in the league. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bet: Vikings ML (-130) & Jones Over 71.5 Rushing Yards (-110)</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-chicago-bears-at-green-bay-packers-1-00-pm-et" class="wp-block-heading">Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers – 1:00 pm ET</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I understand this has been a rough start to the season for the Packers. Green Bay has suffered lopsided losses to Minnesota and Atlanta, and the team was unimpressive in wins over New York and Tampa Bay. However, this is still a very talented football team, and the opportunity to get right back in the picture in the NFC North is there. Chicago is still playing without Caleb Williams, making the Bears’ high-octane offense a lot easier to stop. I’m also not fully bought into the Chicago defense, which is currently No. 8 in EPA/Play Allowed (0.116). We saw Carolina move the ball at will against that unit in Week 1. Are we sure Jordan Love and the Green Bay offense can’t do the same? </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Packers also happen to be 6-4 both straight-up and against the spread as home underdogs under Matt LaFleur. They’re also 27-17 SU against division opponents with him at the helm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I’m not even sure I’d love Chicago in this game with Williams, so grabbing plus-money odds with Green Bay against Tyson Bagent is a no-brainer. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bet: Packers ML (+120) </strong></p>

It's time for Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 5 NFL Betting Hub , where you'll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That's the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we're relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let's get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 5 NFL best bets and Week 5 NFL player props. 

 MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts 
 
 
 

## Philadelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars - 9:30 am ET (London)

There probably won't be anything fun about waking up and backing a life-less Eagles team, but it feels like it must be done. Losing Lane Johnson absolutely hurts a Philadelphia team with a weak offensive line, and the Eagles do come into this one off back-to-back losses. However, last week's loss was a one-score defeat at the hands of a good Los Angeles team, and it just doesn't make sense that the Eagles are now getting more than a touchdown against the Jaguars. 

In many cases, I'm alright with using 2026 numbers to handicap games early in the season. Those would strongly favor the Jaguars, a top-10 team in both offensive and defensive EPA/Play, over the Eagles, a bottom-10 team in both. However, with some of these top-tier franchises, you have to give them some time to figure things out. Well, Philadelphia has been one of the league's better teams for years, and this team is still extremely talented. That said, I can't get on board with writing them off completely. And I'm nowhere close to wrapping my head around Jacksonville moving from -2.5 to -7.5 based on a couple of recent results. 

I'll also throw this out there: Philadelphia is 15-3 straight-up and 10-8 against the spread after a game with a turnover margin of +2 or better under Nick Sirianni. The Eagles are also 6-4 when coming off two or more consecutive losses under Sirianni. 

If anything gives me pause about backing the Eagles, it's that the Jaguars are very used to playing in London. But I still think we'll get a one-score game here. 

 Bet: Eagles +8 (-110 - 1.5 units) & Eagles ML (+320 - 0.5 units) 

## Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints - 1:00 pm ET

I'm a little concerned about the Minnesota passing game right now. Kyler Murray has looked abysmal for the Vikings, and Justin Jefferson is banged up. At some point, Minnesota is going to need to reconsider things at the position, and I'm not even sure it'll look right this week. But I don't think the Vikings need to be explosive through the air to win here. Last week, the Falcons rushed for 205 yards against a soft Saints defensive line, and I imagine Minnesota will similarly pound away between the tackles. Also, the Vikings are No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.209), by far. Once again, Brian Flores is coordinating one of the league's best defenses, and the team should be able to keep New Orleans in check. 

Not only am I playing Vikings moneyline in this one, but I'm also taking Aaron Jones to have at least 72 rushing yards. He has had at least 94 in two of the last three games, and he's now getting a team that is allowing more rushing yards per game to opposing running backs than any other group in the league. 

 Bet: Vikings ML (-130) & Jones Over 71.5 Rushing Yards (-110) 

## Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers - 1:00 pm ET

I understand this has been a rough start to the season for the Packers. Green Bay has suffered lopsided losses to Minnesota and Atlanta, and the team was unimpressive in wins over New York and Tampa Bay. However, this is still a very talented football team, and the opportunity to get right back in the picture in the NFC North is there. Chicago is still playing without Caleb Williams, making the Bears' high-octane offense a lot easier to stop. I'm also not fully bought into the Chicago defense, which is currently No. 8 in EPA/Play Allowed (0.116). We saw Carolina move the ball at will against that unit in Week 1. Are we sure Jordan Love and the Green Bay offense can't do the same? 

The Packers also happen to be 6-4 both straight-up and against the spread as home underdogs under Matt LaFleur. They're also 27-17 SU against division opponents with him at the helm. 

I'm not even sure I'd love Chicago in this game with Williams, so grabbing plus-money odds with Green Bay against Tyson Bagent is a no-brainer. 

 Bet: Packers ML (+120)

<h2 id="h-tuley-s-takes-nfl-week-5" class="wp-block-heading">Tuley’s Takes – NFL Week 5:</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We’re riding high in the Tuley’s Takes home office after a great NFL Week 4, but certainly trying to stay level-headed and not get overconfident heading into Week 5.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Obviously, we all love to win, but I’ve long said it’s important to stay objective and, in our case, continue to follow our “dog or pass” mantra without trying to pick every dog on board when it all looks so easy. We’ll still be selective this week even though, to borrow a baseball phrase, “the ball is looking like a beach ball right now.”</p>
        <div data-stn-player="JnOrSEms"></div>
        <script data-cfasync="false" src="/cdn-cgi/scripts/5c5dd728/cloudflare-static/email-decode.min.js"></script><script async type="text/javascript" src="https://embed.sendtonews.com/player3/embedcode.js?fk=JnOrSEms">
        </script>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I went 4-0-1 ATS with my NFL Best Bets in Week 4 (after going 3-1 ATS in CFB on Saturday; throw in the Metallica concert at the Sphere on Saturday night and my weekend was, as Larry David would say, pretty pretty good!) with wins on the Browns +3 in their 27-24 home upset vs. the Steelers on Thursday Night Football, Patriots +6.5 in their 29-26 road upset at the Bills, Titans +11.5 in their 24-18 loss at the Ravens and Raiders +4.5 in their 30-27 home loss vs. the Chiefs. The push was on the Chargers +7 in their 30-23 loss at the Seahawks. I also went 4-0-1 on my main solo @ViewFromVegas in the Circa Sports Million, and fortunately started the 3-week in-season contest on Weeks 4-6 with a perfect 5-0 in the Westgate/Caesars SuperContest at the Westgate, as they had Chargers +7.5 on the contest card.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">My Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio also went 3-1 with the Cowboys +8.5, Jaguars +8.5 and Falcons +8.5 all winning outright (so we actually didn’t need the added points), and the lone loser on the Broncos +8.5, and Will Lutz missed a FG late that would have won that teaser, too. But you can’t win ‘em all – though we try, right?</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Of course, I’m also aware that I benefitted greatly from underdogs going 10-4-2 ATS overall in Week 4, and in addition to the Chargers’ push being available at +7.5, the Buccaneers push on +3 was also available at +3.5 earlier in the week, so I should’ve had a great week unless I was going something horribly wrong!</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Enough looking back, let’s get to my “takes” on the full NFL Week 5 schedule, which has just 15 games with the Chiefs and Panthers having early bye weeks. For the uninitiated here at Tuley’s Takes, I give my “take” on each game from my “dog or pass” point of view, trying to determine if the underdog is getting enough points to make them a play – or if I recommend passing on the game. I’ll also give my patent-pending Tuley’s Pool Play Percentages for those in contests where you have to pick every game (or just as another helpful handicapping point).</p>



<h2 id="h-tampa-bay-at-dallas-8" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261008NFL00047" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Tampa Bay at Dallas </a>(<a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261008NFL00047" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">-8)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This week’s Thursday Night Football game is pretty much a dud with the Buccaneers at 0-4 and still without Baker Mayfield, but it’s receiving a lot of attention because it’s a standalone game and being projected as one of if not the top Circa Survivor play of this week despite most contestants usually avoiding TNF. I usually love TNF dogs – like the Browns last week – but I can’t quite pull the trigger here on the Bucs even getting more than a TD. The advance line on this game was Cowboys -9.5 and looked like it might go to 10, but it got bet back down to 8 on Tuesday morning. The Bucs defense did step up in Jalon Daniels’ first start as they lost only 17-14 to the Packers, but I don’t have the confidence of the early bettors that they can do it against the Cowboys’ offense. I’m certainly considering the Cowboys on some of my remaining Survivors, but if I’m betting this game I’ll probably just use Cowboys -2 as the opening leg in our Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio to our preferred games on Sunday.   </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Pass, unless Cowboys -2 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Cowboys 55/45 in rare ATS contests that use TNF and all SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-philadelphia-vs-jacksonville-7-5" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00041" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Philadelphia vs. Jacksonville (-7.5) </a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We get another early London game this Sunday (yippee, I slept through the Colts-Commanders game last Sunday after the late Metallica concert).  The advance line for this game was Jaguars -2.5 last week, but that was before they beat the Bengals 22-17 and the Eagles squandered a 10-point lead and lost 24-20 to the Rams. Saquon Barkley pulled a hamstring in the loss and the line reopened Jaguars -3 and was already climbing when the news got worse for the Eagles on Tuesday as Lane Johnson announced his retirement. The line is now up to Jaguars -7.5 at most books as of Wednesday afternoon and -8 at Circa Sports. As hard as it is to back the Eagles right now, that’s too much of an overadjustment and I have to take them getting more than a TD.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Eagles +7.5 or better (Pool Play Percentages: Eagles 67/33 in ATS contests, but Jaguars still 75/25 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-indianapolis-at-pittsburgh-2-5" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00038" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Indianapolis at Pittsburgh (-2.5)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The advance line was Steelers -2.5 and didn’t budge after they lost 27-24 to the Browns last Thursday and the Colts beat the Commanders 30-13 in London. Indy isn’t getting too much credit for that as Washington didn’t have Jaylen Daniels. And it’s hard to take them at the short number with teams coming back from international games with no rest are 10-13 ATS (43.5%), so let’s just toss them in the Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio..</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Colts +8.5 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Colts 55/45 in ATS contests, but Steelers still 60/40 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-minnesota-2-at-new-orleans" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00057" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Minnesota (-2) at New Orleans</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Saints are off to a disappointing 1-3 start while the Vikings are an even more surprising 4-0. Brian Flores’ defense has been the key for Minnesota, allowing just 51 points (12.75 ppg) while the offense is still trying to find itself with Kyler Murray. It’s tempting to use the Saints as another teaser leg, but I think I’m going to pass here in case the Vikings are for real.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Pass (Pool Play Percentages: Vikings 60/40 in all SU and ATS contests)</strong>.</p>



<h2 id="h-cleveland-at-new-york-jets-1-5" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00034" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Cleveland at New York Jets (-1.5)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Do you see how I’m trying to be selective here? That applies to this game as well, as my initial thought was to take the Browns plus any points. The advance line was Jets -2.5, but the Browns won their third straight game on TNF and the Jets lost 23-12 to the Bears and the line understandably reopened Jets -2. It has since been bet down to 1.5, so it’s clear the Browns are a dreaded public dog, and I have to invoke the “pass” part of “dog or pass.” However, I’ll probably use the Browns in some teasers as long as the line doesn’t drop further.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Browns +7.5 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Jets 55/45 in all SU and ATS contests).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-cincinnati-7-at-miami" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00032" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Cincinnati (-7) at Miami</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Dolphins are 0-4 and in the running for the worst record in the league and the No. 1 draft pick, as expected. They were dominated by the Raiders and 49ers in the first two games, but then almost covered +9.5 against the Chiefs in a 24-10 Week loss and then did cover +10.5 this past Sunday in a 15-10 loss at the Vikings (thanks to T.J. Hockenson sliding down short of the goal line, though that’s yet another reason we prefer dogs, as we don’t need to cheer for chalk to score meaningless TDs to cover – and it was the right call, by the way). Anyway, the Dolphins are being more competitive, plus the Bengals are without WRs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins) and will be content to just get out of this game with a W.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Dolphins +7 (Pool Play Percentages: Bengals 60/40 in ATS contests, lower at 6.5 and a pass, but Bengals still 75/25 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-las-vegas-at-new-england-3-5" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00033" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Las Vegas at New England (-3.5)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Raiders fell from the ranks of the unbeaten with their 30-27 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday, but they did cover and are now 4-0 ATS as they continue to exceed preseason expectations. The advance line for this game was Patriots -3 before they turned around their slow start by upsetting the Bills 29-26 in Buffalo. But we’re happy with that as we now get the hook at +3.5 with a live Raiders team.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Raiders +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Raiders 67/33 in ATS contests, but Patriots still 67/33 in SU pools – do you see what I did there? I’m basically saying if they were to play this game three times that the Raiders would win outright one time, the Patriots would cover one time and the Patriots would win by 3 and not cover one time, and we’ll see this in a couple of other games this weekend)</strong>.</p>



<h2 id="h-new-york-giants-at-washington-3-5" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00050" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">New York Giants at Washington (-3.5)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This game looks the same to me as Raiders-Patriots. The advance line was also -3 and now up to -3.5, though in this case mostly driven by the return of Washington QB Jaylen Daniels after missing the 30-13 loss to the Colts in London and falling to 1-3. I’m not sure the right team is favored here with the Giants (3-1) coming off back-to-back albeit non-dominating wins over the Titans and Cardinals. Jameis Winston isn’t lighting up the stat sheet like he usually does, but he’s doing enough to keep the Giants winning (at least against teams in the lower half of the league) as long as he can limit the INTs (and pick sixes).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Giants +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Giants 67/33 in ATS contests, but Commanders still 67/33 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-houston-7-5-at-tennessee" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00042" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Houston (-7.5) at Tennessee</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The advance line for this game was Texans -6.5 but has crossed the key number of 7 despite them falling to 0-4 with their 34-30 loss to the Cowboys and the Titans losing 24-18 to the Ravens (after Lamar Jackson suffered a left ankle sprain). I was lucky to go 2-0 ATS with the Dolphins and Titans in Week 4, and, yes, I’m backing both again, this time as home dogs as I certainly don’t think the winless Texans should be favored by more than a touchdown on the road against anyone despite how many people expect them to get off the schnied here.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Titans +7.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Titans 67/33 in ATS contests, but Texans 80/20 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-chicago-2-5-at-green-bay" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00053" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Chicago (-2.5) at Green Bay</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Packers were 2-point favorites in the advance line last week, but after barely getting by the winless Buccaneers 17-14 and the Bears beating the Jets 23-12 with their third different starting QB in four games, the line flipped to the Bears as short road favorites. I’m high on this Bears team, but I wasn’t thrilled with the switch from Case Keenum to Tyson Bagent and they didn’t look as sharp this past Sunday as they kinda went through the motions in beating the Jets. I’m also not sure this line adjustment is warranted, but still too short for me to take the Packers ATS, so in the Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio they go.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Packers +8.5 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Packers 55/45 in ATS contests, but Bears still 65/35 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-denver-3-5-at-los-angeles-chargers" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00046" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Denver (-3.5) at Los Angeles Chargers</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Moving to the Sunday afternoon slate, this was supposed to be a battle of AFC West contenders, but the Chargers are off to an 0-4 start. The advance line for this game was -2.5 but has also crossed the key number of 3 after both teams lost this past Sunday. I’m sure the Broncos were hoping to be better than 2-2, but they’re a little lucky they’re not 1-3, as they could have lost to either the Jaguars or Rams, too. Despite being winless, the Chargers have been playing better in their losses to the Bills and Seahawks, as they should’ve at least covered at the Bills and did push at the Seahawks. They don’t have much of a home-field advantage in L.A., but they should be able to take this to the wire as well and hopefully just stay within a FG.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Chargers +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Chargers 67/33 in ATS contests, but Broncos still 67/33 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-san-francisco-at-seattle-3" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00061" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">San Francisco at Seattle (-3)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The advance line for this NFC West battle was Seahawks -3.5 last week (I wish I had grabbed the 49ers +3.5 then), but settled at 3 after the 49ers beat the Broncos 24-14 and the Seahawks beat the Chargers 30-23. The 49ers (4-0) lead the defending Super Bowl champions by a game in the division, so this is a key early-season matchup, especially with the Rams scuffling at 1-3. As I said, we missed the value at +3.5 and have to pass just getting the 3.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Pass (Pool Play Percentages: 49ers 55/45 in ATS contests on principle, but Seahawks still 65/35 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-detroit-5-5-at-arizona" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00059" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Detroit (-5.5) at Arizona</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I’m really conflicted on this game. Like last year, I was high on the Lions making a Super Bowl run, but they greatly disappointed last year by missing the playoffs and are off to a mediocre 2-2 start this season. I still have a hard time fading them and miss out on the Panthers +3.5 on Sunday night as Carolina won 32-26. The Cardinals are 1-3, but 2-2 ATS with their upset of the Chargers in Week 1 and covering vs. the 49ers in Week 3. I’m tempted to take the points here, but can’t pull the trigger as I feel I’ve played enough dogs this week in trying to be selective, and this wouldn’t be in my Top 5 or 6.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Pass (Pool Play Percentages: Cardinals 55/45 in ATS contests on principle, but Lions still 67/33 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-baltimore-at-atlanta-3-5" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261011NFL00055" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Baltimore at Atlanta (-3.5)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The advance line for this Sunday nighter was Ravens -6.5, but then Lamar Jackson was hurt in the Ravens’ non-covering 24-18 win over the Titans and the Falcons upset the Saints 45-24 on Monday night and the line has gone all the way to the Falcons being favored by more than a FG. The Falcons seem to love primetime and I was happy to be on them in their 35-14 upset of the Packers a week ago Thursday, but this is too much of a line overadjustment. Tyler Huntley is a poor man’s Jackson and knows this Baltimore offense. It would certainly not be a shocking upset, but I’ll gladly take the bonus points.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Ravens +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Ravens 67/33 in ATS contests, but Falcons still 67/33 in SU pools).</strong></p>



<h2 id="h-buffalo-at-los-angeles-rams-3" class="wp-block-heading"><a href="https://data.vsin.com/nfl/matchups/game/20261012NFL00062" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Buffalo at Los Angeles Rams (-3)</a></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This had all the makings of a Super Bowl preview in Week 3, but the Rams, the preseason future-book favorites, are off to a 2-2 start (and lucky not to be 1-3 after needing to rally late to beat the Eagles) and desperate to get back on the winning track and in the playoff hunt. The advance line was Rams -2 and has risen to 3 after their win and the Bills’ first loss of the season to the Patriots. If this were to get to 3.5 (not likely as several books have the +3 shaded to -115), I would take the Bills, but otherwise need to pass. However, I will consider adding the Bills +9 to some teasers from Sunday’s games. If I don’t have too many live teasers to this game, the one-game tease would be Bills +9 and Over 48.5 as it should be a shootout regardless.   </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Best Bet: Bills +9 in teasers, possibly with Over 48.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Bills 55/45 in ATS contests, but Rams still 65/35 in SU pools).</strong></p>

## Tuley's Takes - NFL Week 5:

We’re riding high in the Tuley’s Takes home office after a great NFL Week 4, but certainly trying to stay level-headed and not get overconfident heading into Week 5. 

Obviously, we all love to win, but I’ve long said it’s important to stay objective and, in our case, continue to follow our “dog or pass” mantra without trying to pick every dog on board when it all looks so easy. We’ll still be selective this week even though, to borrow a baseball phrase, “the ball is looking like a beach ball right now.” 
 
 
 

I went 4-0-1 ATS with my NFL Best Bets in Week 4 (after going 3-1 ATS in CFB on Saturday; throw in the Metallica concert at the Sphere on Saturday night and my weekend was, as Larry David would say, pretty pretty good!) with wins on the Browns +3 in their 27-24 home upset vs. the Steelers on Thursday Night Football, Patriots +6.5 in their 29-26 road upset at the Bills, Titans +11.5 in their 24-18 loss at the Ravens and Raiders +4.5 in their 30-27 home loss vs. the Chiefs. The push was on the Chargers +7 in their 30-23 loss at the Seahawks. I also went 4-0-1 on my main solo @ViewFromVegas in the Circa Sports Million, and fortunately started the 3-week in-season contest on Weeks 4-6 with a perfect 5-0 in the Westgate/Caesars SuperContest at the Westgate, as they had Chargers +7.5 on the contest card. 

My Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio also went 3-1 with the Cowboys +8.5, Jaguars +8.5 and Falcons +8.5 all winning outright (so we actually didn’t need the added points), and the lone loser on the Broncos +8.5, and Will Lutz missed a FG late that would have won that teaser, too. But you can’t win ‘em all – though we try, right? 

Of course, I’m also aware that I benefitted greatly from underdogs going 10-4-2 ATS overall in Week 4, and in addition to the Chargers’ push being available at +7.5, the Buccaneers push on +3 was also available at +3.5 earlier in the week, so I should’ve had a great week unless I was going something horribly wrong! 

Enough looking back, let’s get to my “takes” on the full NFL Week 5 schedule, which has just 15 games with the Chiefs and Panthers having early bye weeks. For the uninitiated here at Tuley’s Takes, I give my “take” on each game from my “dog or pass” point of view, trying to determine if the underdog is getting enough points to make them a play – or if I recommend passing on the game. I’ll also give my patent-pending Tuley’s Pool Play Percentages for those in contests where you have to pick every game (or just as another helpful handicapping point). 

## Tampa Bay at Dallas ( -8) 

This week’s Thursday Night Football game is pretty much a dud with the Buccaneers at 0-4 and still without Baker Mayfield, but it’s receiving a lot of attention because it’s a standalone game and being projected as one of if not the top Circa Survivor play of this week despite most contestants usually avoiding TNF. I usually love TNF dogs – like the Browns last week – but I can’t quite pull the trigger here on the Bucs even getting more than a TD. The advance line on this game was Cowboys -9.5 and looked like it might go to 10, but it got bet back down to 8 on Tuesday morning. The Bucs defense did step up in Jalon Daniels’ first start as they lost only 17-14 to the Packers, but I don’t have the confidence of the early bettors that they can do it against the Cowboys’ offense. I’m certainly considering the Cowboys on some of my remaining Survivors, but if I’m betting this game I’ll probably just use Cowboys -2 as the opening leg in our Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio to our preferred games on Sunday. 

 Best Bet: Pass, unless Cowboys -2 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Cowboys 55/45 in rare ATS contests that use TNF and all SU pools). 

## Philadelphia vs. Jacksonville (-7.5)  

We get another early London game this Sunday (yippee, I slept through the Colts-Commanders game last Sunday after the late Metallica concert). The advance line for this game was Jaguars -2.5 last week, but that was before they beat the Bengals 22-17 and the Eagles squandered a 10-point lead and lost 24-20 to the Rams. Saquon Barkley pulled a hamstring in the loss and the line reopened Jaguars -3 and was already climbing when the news got worse for the Eagles on Tuesday as Lane Johnson announced his retirement. The line is now up to Jaguars -7.5 at most books as of Wednesday afternoon and -8 at Circa Sports. As hard as it is to back the Eagles right now, that’s too much of an overadjustment and I have to take them getting more than a TD. 

 Best Bet: Eagles +7.5 or better (Pool Play Percentages: Eagles 67/33 in ATS contests, but Jaguars still 75/25 in SU pools). 

## Indianapolis at Pittsburgh (-2.5) 

The advance line was Steelers -2.5 and didn’t budge after they lost 27-24 to the Browns last Thursday and the Colts beat the Commanders 30-13 in London. Indy isn’t getting too much credit for that as Washington didn’t have Jaylen Daniels. And it’s hard to take them at the short number with teams coming back from international games with no rest are 10-13 ATS (43.5%), so let’s just toss them in the Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio.. 

 Best Bet: Colts +8.5 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Colts 55/45 in ATS contests, but Steelers still 60/40 in SU pools). 

## Minnesota (-2) at New Orleans 

The Saints are off to a disappointing 1-3 start while the Vikings are an even more surprising 4-0. Brian Flores’ defense has been the key for Minnesota, allowing just 51 points (12.75 ppg) while the offense is still trying to find itself with Kyler Murray. It’s tempting to use the Saints as another teaser leg, but I think I’m going to pass here in case the Vikings are for real. 

 Best Bet: Pass (Pool Play Percentages: Vikings 60/40 in all SU and ATS contests) . 

## Cleveland at New York Jets (-1.5) 

Do you see how I’m trying to be selective here? That applies to this game as well, as my initial thought was to take the Browns plus any points. The advance line was Jets -2.5, but the Browns won their third straight game on TNF and the Jets lost 23-12 to the Bears and the line understandably reopened Jets -2. It has since been bet down to 1.5, so it’s clear the Browns are a dreaded public dog, and I have to invoke the “pass” part of “dog or pass.” However, I’ll probably use the Browns in some teasers as long as the line doesn’t drop further. 

 Best Bet: Browns +7.5 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Jets 55/45 in all SU and ATS contests). 

## Cincinnati (-7) at Miami 

The Dolphins are 0-4 and in the running for the worst record in the league and the No. 1 draft pick, as expected. They were dominated by the Raiders and 49ers in the first two games, but then almost covered +9.5 against the Chiefs in a 24-10 Week loss and then did cover +10.5 this past Sunday in a 15-10 loss at the Vikings (thanks to T.J. Hockenson sliding down short of the goal line, though that’s yet another reason we prefer dogs, as we don’t need to cheer for chalk to score meaningless TDs to cover – and it was the right call, by the way). Anyway, the Dolphins are being more competitive, plus the Bengals are without WRs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins) and will be content to just get out of this game with a W. 

 Best Bet: Dolphins +7 (Pool Play Percentages: Bengals 60/40 in ATS contests, lower at 6.5 and a pass, but Bengals still 75/25 in SU pools). 

## Las Vegas at New England (-3.5) 

The Raiders fell from the ranks of the unbeaten with their 30-27 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday, but they did cover and are now 4-0 ATS as they continue to exceed preseason expectations. The advance line for this game was Patriots -3 before they turned around their slow start by upsetting the Bills 29-26 in Buffalo. But we’re happy with that as we now get the hook at +3.5 with a live Raiders team. 

 Best Bet: Raiders +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Raiders 67/33 in ATS contests, but Patriots still 67/33 in SU pools – do you see what I did there? I’m basically saying if they were to play this game three times that the Raiders would win outright one time, the Patriots would cover one time and the Patriots would win by 3 and not cover one time, and we’ll see this in a couple of other games this weekend) . 

## New York Giants at Washington (-3.5) 

This game looks the same to me as Raiders-Patriots. The advance line was also -3 and now up to -3.5, though in this case mostly driven by the return of Washington QB Jaylen Daniels after missing the 30-13 loss to the Colts in London and falling to 1-3. I’m not sure the right team is favored here with the Giants (3-1) coming off back-to-back albeit non-dominating wins over the Titans and Cardinals. Jameis Winston isn’t lighting up the stat sheet like he usually does, but he’s doing enough to keep the Giants winning (at least against teams in the lower half of the league) as long as he can limit the INTs (and pick sixes). 

 Best Bet: Giants +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Giants 67/33 in ATS contests, but Commanders still 67/33 in SU pools). 

## Houston (-7.5) at Tennessee 

The advance line for this game was Texans -6.5 but has crossed the key number of 7 despite them falling to 0-4 with their 34-30 loss to the Cowboys and the Titans losing 24-18 to the Ravens (after Lamar Jackson suffered a left ankle sprain). I was lucky to go 2-0 ATS with the Dolphins and Titans in Week 4, and, yes, I’m backing both again, this time as home dogs as I certainly don’t think the winless Texans should be favored by more than a touchdown on the road against anyone despite how many people expect them to get off the schnied here. 

 Best Bet: Titans +7.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Titans 67/33 in ATS contests, but Texans 80/20 in SU pools). 

## Chicago (-2.5) at Green Bay 

The Packers were 2-point favorites in the advance line last week, but after barely getting by the winless Buccaneers 17-14 and the Bears beating the Jets 23-12 with their third different starting QB in four games, the line flipped to the Bears as short road favorites. I’m high on this Bears team, but I wasn’t thrilled with the switch from Case Keenum to Tyson Bagent and they didn’t look as sharp this past Sunday as they kinda went through the motions in beating the Jets. I’m also not sure this line adjustment is warranted, but still too short for me to take the Packers ATS, so in the Tuley’s Teaser Portfolio they go. 

 Best Bet: Packers +8.5 in teasers (Pool Play Percentages: Packers 55/45 in ATS contests, but Bears still 65/35 in SU pools). 

## Denver (-3.5) at Los Angeles Chargers 

Moving to the Sunday afternoon slate, this was supposed to be a battle of AFC West contenders, but the Chargers are off to an 0-4 start. The advance line for this game was -2.5 but has also crossed the key number of 3 after both teams lost this past Sunday. I’m sure the Broncos were hoping to be better than 2-2, but they’re a little lucky they’re not 1-3, as they could have lost to either the Jaguars or Rams, too. Despite being winless, the Chargers have been playing better in their losses to the Bills and Seahawks, as they should’ve at least covered at the Bills and did push at the Seahawks. They don’t have much of a home-field advantage in L.A., but they should be able to take this to the wire as well and hopefully just stay within a FG. 

 Best Bet: Chargers +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Chargers 67/33 in ATS contests, but Broncos still 67/33 in SU pools). 

## San Francisco at Seattle (-3) 

The advance line for this NFC West battle was Seahawks -3.5 last week (I wish I had grabbed the 49ers +3.5 then), but settled at 3 after the 49ers beat the Broncos 24-14 and the Seahawks beat the Chargers 30-23. The 49ers (4-0) lead the defending Super Bowl champions by a game in the division, so this is a key early-season matchup, especially with the Rams scuffling at 1-3. As I said, we missed the value at +3.5 and have to pass just getting the 3. 

 Best Bet: Pass (Pool Play Percentages: 49ers 55/45 in ATS contests on principle, but Seahawks still 65/35 in SU pools). 

## Detroit (-5.5) at Arizona 

I’m really conflicted on this game. Like last year, I was high on the Lions making a Super Bowl run, but they greatly disappointed last year by missing the playoffs and are off to a mediocre 2-2 start this season. I still have a hard time fading them and miss out on the Panthers +3.5 on Sunday night as Carolina won 32-26. The Cardinals are 1-3, but 2-2 ATS with their upset of the Chargers in Week 1 and covering vs. the 49ers in Week 3. I’m tempted to take the points here, but can’t pull the trigger as I feel I’ve played enough dogs this week in trying to be selective, and this wouldn’t be in my Top 5 or 6. 

 Best Bet: Pass (Pool Play Percentages: Cardinals 55/45 in ATS contests on principle, but Lions still 67/33 in SU pools). 

## Baltimore at Atlanta (-3.5) 

The advance line for this Sunday nighter was Ravens -6.5, but then Lamar Jackson was hurt in the Ravens’ non-covering 24-18 win over the Titans and the Falcons upset the Saints 45-24 on Monday night and the line has gone all the way to the Falcons being favored by more than a FG. The Falcons seem to love primetime and I was happy to be on them in their 35-14 upset of the Packers a week ago Thursday, but this is too much of a line overadjustment. Tyler Huntley is a poor man’s Jackson and knows this Baltimore offense. It would certainly not be a shocking upset, but I’ll gladly take the bonus points. 

 Best Bet: Ravens +3.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Ravens 67/33 in ATS contests, but Falcons still 67/33 in SU pools). 

## Buffalo at Los Angeles Rams (-3) 

This had all the makings of a Super Bowl preview in Week 3, but the Rams, the preseason future-book favorites, are off to a 2-2 start (and lucky not to be 1-3 after needing to rally late to beat the Eagles) and desperate to get back on the winning track and in the playoff hunt. The advance line was Rams -2 and has risen to 3 after their win and the Bills’ first loss of the season to the Patriots. If this were to get to 3.5 (not likely as several books have the +3 shaded to -115), I would take the Bills, but otherwise need to pass. However, I will consider adding the Bills +9 to some teasers from Sunday’s games. If I don’t have too many live teasers to this game, the one-game tease would be Bills +9 and Over 48.5 as it should be a shootout regardless. 

 Best Bet: Bills +9 in teasers, possibly with Over 48.5 (Pool Play Percentages: Bills 55/45 in ATS contests, but Rams still 65/35 in SU pools).

<h2 id="h-nfl-week-5-best-bets-predictions-and-picks-from-steve-makinen" class="wp-block-heading">NFL Week 5 Best Bets, Predictions and Picks from Steve Makinen:</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">I’ve been on a nice roll lately in the NFL, although my 7-2-1 ATS record on best bets in Week 4 came up a half game shy of my Week 3 record. That said, as I move on to Week 5’s game, my season record is now 25-12-1 ATS (67.6%). This week’s games are highlighted by the NFC West action: the 49ers and Seahawks meet in a big one on Sunday afternoon, and the Rams host the Bills on Monday night in what many sources are calling a Super Bowl preview. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you were on the VSiN website earlier in the week, you may have seen my NFL article, <a href="https://vsin.com/nfl/steve-makinen-new-nfl-betting-systems-for-the-2026-season/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><em>New NFL Betting Systems for the 2026 Season</em></a>, where we added several new team strength, streak, and last-game stat systems to our Analytics Reports. They’ve been a huge part of my early success, and I’ll keep leaning on them going forward. After digging through the Week 5 report, I’ve landed on these games for this weekend.</p>
